findings.evidence: The claim under test is 'three successive attempts to explain WHICH mechanism empties the bound set each shipped a false clause'. (A) Its own cited source contradicts it. claude-workflow-plugin-71n7's comment of 2026-10-01T12:23:28Z (checked clean against .beads/quarantine.tsv) enumerates exactly three attempts and says of the third -- 'The causes are independently sufficient, with truncation preempting' -- 'This one is believed true'. Under the author's own enumeration, 2 of 3 shipped a false clause, not 3 of 3; and that third account never shipped at all, it is the one deleted instead of attempted a fourth time. (B) Independently, on the enumeration of texts that ACTUALLY shipped and were reviewed (T1 = fe278a8's own, T2 = round 2's subject, T3 = round 3's subject), T1 is vindicated by round 3's own measurement. T1 read 'G.1's successful approve TRUNCATES $TRACKING, so by this point the epic's recorded completion declares files that are no longer in the change set an approval would bind' (verbatim from this diff's removed lines). docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-paj9-r3.json, R3-F1 evidence: 'line 657's approve SUCCEEDS (the test's own G.1/G.1b assert status=approved, exit 0), so truncate_changed_files_tracker RUNS and empties the tracker; only THEN does line 675 write the artifact path'; and R3-F1's finding text: 'truncation runs FIRST ... and is what removes src/a.sh'. T1 names the mechanism that actually fires first and is independently sufficient. It is INCOMPLETE (silent on overdetermination by the line-675 write) but it is not false. (C) 71n7's own rationale for calling T1 false re-commits the exact non-sequitur R3-F1 refuted: it argues 'FALSE as an attribution -- round 2 measured declared=1 bound=1 matched=0 with the tracker NON-EMPTY', but R3-F1 established that 'bound=1 does not discriminate between the two hypotheses at all' (Variant Y: changing line 675 from > to >> gave byte-identical output), and the measurement is round 1's, not round 2's -- docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-paj9-r1.json carries it verbatim ('bound=1 matched=0) ... Declared (first 12 shown): src/a.sh', 'The tracker AT THAT MOMENT held exactly one path: docs/specs/<epic>.md') while r2.json contains zero occurrences of 'declared=' or 'total_miss'. Both readings (A) and (B) independently make 'each' false, so the finding does not depend on adjudicating T1.
findings.description: The reduction deleted a falsifiable CAUSAL account and replaced it with a falsifiable HISTORICAL one, and the replacement is the new false claim. This is the one sentence the reduction introduced that a future reader acts on: it is the stated justification for never attempting a causal account again, and it is wrong in the direction that discards a CORRECT explanation -- the account 71n7 itself marks 'believed true'. A reader who follows the pointer the same sentence supplies finds the pointer's own content contradicting the sentence's summary of it. Graded HIGH strictly under the operator's pre-registered stop rule for this round ('makes a shipped claim FALSE -> HIGH'), applied to a round whose framing is explicitly 'is every surviving claim true' and 'whether the REDUCTION introduced anything false'. Stated plainly for proportion: NO gate behaviour, assertion, exit code, error key or test semantic is misstated by it -- design-rollup.test.sh is 73/73 and every claim about the gate in this block is verified true. Remedy, deletion-preferring per the principle this round adopted: cut the characterisation and keep only the uncontested cost statement 71n7 already carries ('by this point the comment had cost three review rounds'), e.g. '...why the causal account that used to sit here was removed: it cost three review rounds and is not load-bearing -- the warning above is.' That removes a claim rather than adding a fourth one to be wrong about.

findings.description: Same shape as R4-F1 and introduced by the same reduction: a historical count of three where the record supports two. Graded MEDIUM rather than HIGH because I can show only that round 2's artifact does not RECORD the measurement, not that round 2 never ran it -- a reviewer may measure without reporting, so unlike R4-F1 I cannot affirmatively disprove the sentence. What a reader CAN check is the artifacts, and they show two. The underlying warning is true and strongly measured regardless, so nothing about the seed's necessity is in doubt.
